<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

        (∀ (i : Fin n), Iff (List.instMembership.mem order i) (Ne i k)) →
          Exists fun C =>
            Exists fun ε =>
              And (Real.instLE.le 0 C)
                (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 ε)
                  (∀ (u : Real),
                    Real.instLT.lt 0 u →
                      Real.instLT.lt u ε →
                        ∀ (subError expError addError divError : Fin n → Real),
                          (∀ (i : Fin n), Real.instLE.le (abs (subError i)) u) →
                            (∀ (i : Fin n), Real.instLE.le (abs (expError i)) u) →
                              (∀ (i : Fin n), Real.instLE.le (abs (addError i)) u) →
                                (∀ (i : Fin n), Real.instLE.le (abs (divError i)) u) →
                                  Real.instLE.le
                                    (instHDiv.hDiv
                                      (Pi.normedRing.norm fun i =>
                                        instHSub.hSub
                                          (LocalDef001 x k order subError expError addError
                                            divError i)
                                          (LocalDef002 x k order i))
                                      (Pi.normedRing.norm fun i => LocalDef002 x k order i))
                                    (instHAdd.hAdd
                                      (instHMul.hMul
                                        (instHAdd.hAdd (instHAdd.hAdd n.cast 2)
                                          (instHMul.hMul 2 (instHSub.hSub (x k) (LocalDef003 x))))
                                        u)
                                      (instHMul.hMul C (instHPow.hPow u 2)))))"}}

  "role": "blind-translation",
  "semantic_sha256": "83a46baa94f0f181320d669336ade132663e8f3793e0d9afaa2dba36b90c1dc0",
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify n∈ℕ, x:Fin n→ℝ, k∈Fin n, and a finite list L of elements of Fin n, in that order.",
      "After imposing the hypotheses on n, x, k, and L, existentially quantify real constants C and ε. These constants may depend on those fixed data.",
      "For those same C and ε, universally quantify every real u with 0<u<ε.",
      "For each such u, universally quantify four functions s,e,a,d:Fin n→ℝ, corresponding respectively to subError, expError, addError, and divError.",
      "Every coordinate error hypothesis and every coordinate in the output vectors ranges over all i∈Fin n, including i=k."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "There exist C≥0 and ε>0 such that, for every 0<u<ε and every four error functions satisfying the componentwise bounds, ‖q−p‖∞ / ‖p‖∞ ≤ (n+2+2(x_k−m(x)))u + C u².",
      "Here n in the real-valued coefficient is the natural number n embedded in ℝ, and u² is its ordinary second natural power.",
      "The same C and ε work for all permitted u and all permitted error functions for the fixed n, x, k, and L. The theorem does not require a common choice across different input vectors, dimensions, maximizing indices, or summation orders."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "n≥2.",
      "For every i∈Fin n, x_i≤x_k; thus k is an index attaining a maximum, with ties allowed.",
      "L has no duplicate entries.",
      "For every i∈Fin n, i occurs in L if and only if i≠k. Consequently L lists exactly the n−1 other indices in an arbitrary order.",
      "The universally quantified perturbation radius satisfies 0<u<ε.",
      "For every i∈Fin n, |s_i|≤u, |e_i|≤u, |a_i|≤u, and |d_i|≤u."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin n={0,…,n−1}. Write x_i=x(i), and similarly for each error function.",
      "m(x)=inf{x_i:i∈Fin n}=min_i x_i under n≥2. Since k is maximizing, x_k−m(x)=max_i x_i−min_i x_i.",
      "The exact shifted weights are z_i=exp(x_i−x_k), so z_k=1 and every z_i is positive.",
      "The exact denominator is D=1+Σ_{j in L}z_j. The exact output is p_i=z_i/D. Under the list hypotheses, D=Σ_i z_i and p_i=exp(x_i)/Σ_j exp(x_j).",
      "The perturbed weights are w_i=exp((x_i−x_k)(1+s_i))(1+e_i). In particular w_k=1+e_k.",
      "For any list, define A(w,a,[])=0. For nonempty L=[j₁,…,j_r], initialize S₁=w_{j₁}; then for t=2,…,r set S_t=(S_{t−1}+w_{j_t})(1+a_{j_t}); define A(w,a,L)=S_r.",
      "For the target, r=n−1, so the accumulation performs n−2 perturbed additions. The error a_{j₁} is unused, as is a_k. When n=2, no addition-error factor is used.",
      "The perturbed denominator is D̂=1+A(w,a,L), and the output is q_i=(w_i/D̂)(1+d_i). There is no separate perturbation on the final addition of 1. The denominator uses an exact 1 for the omitted index k, while the numerator at k uses w_k.",
      "For v:Fin n→ℝ, ‖v‖∞=max_i|v_i|. Thus the relative error is max_i|q_i−p_i| divided by max_i|p_i|. Since z_k=1 is a maximal weight, ‖p‖∞=p_k=1/D>0.",
      "All operations are real operations, with perturbations introduced only by the displayed factors. Real division in Lean is total, with a/0=0."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "Fix any real vector of dimension at least two, a maximizing coordinate k, and any duplicate-free ordering of all coordinates other than k. Form its exact exponential normalization using shifts by x_k. Form a perturbed output by relatively perturbing each shifted subtraction and exponential value, sequentially accumulating the other-coordinate weights with the specified relative addition errors, adding an exact 1 to that sum, and relatively perturbing each final division. There exist a nonnegative constant C and a positive radius ε, depending on the fixed data, such that whenever all four kinds of coordinate error have magnitude at most u with 0<u<ε, the relative maximum-norm output error is at most (n+2+2(max_i x_i−min_i x_i))u+C u²."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "For n<2 the implication has no admissible hypotheses; for n=0 there is also no index k∈Fin n. The substantive assertion concerns n≥2.",
    "For n≥2 the structural hypotheses are satisfiable: a finite real vector has a maximizing index, and its remaining indices can be listed without repetition.",
    "The quantification over small positive u is not empty because ε>0. For every permitted u, the four zero error functions satisfy all error bounds, so the error hypotheses are also satisfiable.",
    "The reference denominator and ‖p‖∞ are strictly positive, so the relative-error expression is not made trivial by Lean's convention for division by zero.",
    "No explicit nonzero hypothesis is imposed on the perturbed denominator. However, when u<1 the factors 1+e_i and 1+a_i are positive, making the accumulated sum positive and D̂>0. Any witnesses can be restricted to a radius at most 1, so total division does not force a degeneracy near zero error.",
    "The existential remainder constant cannot be chosen separately for each u or error realization. Consequently C u² does not make the first-order coefficient vacuous, although the theorem gives no quantitative size for C or ε.",
    "Bounds on unused error entries, including a_k and the first listed addition error, remain formal hypotheses even though those values cannot affect the output."
  ]
}

  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify n∈ℕ, x:Fin n→ℝ, k∈Fin n, and a finite list L of elements of Fin n, in that order.",
      "After imposing the hypotheses on n, x, k, and L, existentially quantify real constants C and ε. These constants may depend on those fixed data.",
      "For those same C and ε, universally quantify every real u with 0<u<ε.",
      "For each such u, universally quantify four functions s,e,a,d:Fin n→ℝ, corresponding respectively to subError, expError, addError, and divError.",
      "Every coordinate error hypothesis and every coordinate in the output vectors ranges over all i∈Fin n, including i=k."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "There exist C≥0 and ε>0 such that, for every 0<u<ε and every four error functions satisfying the componentwise bounds, ‖q−p‖∞ / ‖p‖∞ ≤ (n+2+2(x_k−m(x)))u + C u².",
      "Here n in the real-valued coefficient is the natural number n embedded in ℝ, and u² is its ordinary second natural power.",
      "The same C and ε work for all permitted u and all permitted error functions for the fixed n, x, k, and L. The theorem does not require a common choice across different input vectors, dimensions, maximizing indices, or summation orders."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "n≥2.",
      "For every i∈Fin n, x_i≤x_k; thus k is an index attaining a maximum, with ties allowed.",
      "L has no duplicate entries.",
      "For every i∈Fin n, i occurs in L if and only if i≠k. Consequently L lists exactly the n−1 other indices in an arbitrary order.",
      "The universally quantified perturbation radius satisfies 0<u<ε.",
      "For every i∈Fin n, |s_i|≤u, |e_i|≤u, |a_i|≤u, and |d_i|≤u."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin n={0,…,n−1}. Write x_i=x(i), and similarly for each error function.",
      "m(x)=inf{x_i:i∈Fin n}=min_i x_i under n≥2. Since k is maximizing, x_k−m(x)=max_i x_i−min_i x_i.",
      "The exact shifted weights are z_i=exp(x_i−x_k), so z_k=1 and every z_i is positive.",
      "The exact denominator is D=1+Σ_{j in L}z_j. The exact output is p_i=z_i/D. Under the list hypotheses, D=Σ_i z_i and p_i=exp(x_i)/Σ_j exp(x_j).",
      "The perturbed weights are w_i=exp((x_i−x_k)(1+s_i))(1+e_i). In particular w_k=1+e_k.",
      "For any list, define A(w,a,[])=0. For nonempty L=[j₁,…,j_r], initialize S₁=w_{j₁}; then for t=2,…,r set S_t=(S_{t−1}+w_{j_t})(1+a_{j_t}); define A(w,a,L)=S_r.",
      "For the target, r=n−1, so the accumulation performs n−2 perturbed additions. The error a_{j₁} is unused, as is a_k. When n=2, no addition-error factor is used.",
      "The perturbed denominator is D̂=1+A(w,a,L), and the output is q_i=(w_i/D̂)(1+d_i). There is no separate perturbation on the final addition of 1. The denominator uses an exact 1 for the omitted index k, while the numerator at k uses w_k.",
      "For v:Fin n→ℝ, ‖v‖∞=max_i|v_i|. Thus the relative error is max_i|q_i−p_i| divided by max_i|p_i|. Since z_k=1 is a maximal weight, ‖p‖∞=p_k=1/D>0.",
      "All operations are real operations, with perturbations introduced only by the displayed factors. Real division in Lean is total, with a/0=0."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "Fix any real vector of dimension at least two, a maximizing coordinate k, and any duplicate-free ordering of all coordinates other than k. Form its exact exponential normalization using shifts by x_k. Form a perturbed output by relatively perturbing each shifted subtraction and exponential value, sequentially accumulating the other-coordinate weights with the specified relative addition errors, adding an exact 1 to that sum, and relatively perturbing each final division. There exist a nonnegative constant C and a positive radius ε, depending on the fixed data, such that whenever all four kinds of coordinate error have magnitude at most u with 0<u<ε, the relative maximum-norm output error is at most (n+2+2(max_i x_i−min_i x_i))u+C u²."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "For n<2 the implication has no admissible hypotheses; for n=0 there is also no index k∈Fin n. The substantive assertion concerns n≥2.",
    "For n≥2 the structural hypotheses are satisfiable: a finite real vector has a maximizing index, and its remaining indices can be listed without repetition.",
    "The quantification over small positive u is not empty because ε>0. For every permitted u, the four zero error functions satisfy all error bounds, so the error hypotheses are also satisfiable.",
    "The reference denominator and ‖p‖∞ are strictly positive, so the relative-error expression is not made trivial by Lean's convention for division by zero.",
    "No explicit nonzero hypothesis is imposed on the perturbed denominator. However, when u<1 the factors 1+e_i and 1+a_i are positive, making the accumulated sum positive and D̂>0. Any witnesses can be restricted to a radius at most 1, so total division does not force a degeneracy near zero error.",
    "The existential remainder constant cannot be chosen separately for each u or error realization. Consequently C u² does not make the first-order coefficient vacuous, although the theorem gives no quantitative size for C or ε.",
    "Bounds on unused error entries, including a_k and the first listed addition error, remain formal hypotheses even though those values cannot affect the output."
  ]
}
